topic_title: 1H NMR — Chemical Shift, Integration and Splitting

notes_list.title: 1H NMR — Chemical Shift, Integration and Splitting
notes_list.basic_overview: 1H NMR reports proton environments through chemical shift, integration and spin-spin coupling. Together they provide connectivity and local environment information.
notes_list.extra_info_content: Chemical shift reflects shielding/deshielding; integration estimates relative proton count; splitting follows coupling to nonequivalent neighboring nuclei under first-order conditions.
notes_list.examples: Ethyl group often gives triplet/quartet patterns in simple first-order spectra; aldehydic protons appear far downfield compared with simple alkyl protons.
notes_list.conditions_and_medium: Deuterated solvents are used; TMS or another reference sets the chemical-shift scale. Exchangeable OH/NH signals can broaden or shift with solvent and temperature.
notes_list.mechanism_steps: Apply: number of signals → integration → multiplicity → coupling constants → chemical shift → connect fragments.
notes_list.kinetics_and_energy: For simple first-order systems, n equivalent neighboring protons often give n+1 lines. Coupling is governed by spin-spin interactions and depends on geometry.
notes_list.common_traps: n+1 is not universal; complex/second-order spectra, equivalent nuclei and long-range couplings can violate the simple rule.

exam_focus.level: IIT-JAM / MSc entrance / GATE concept depth
must_revise: Δν and J must be distinguished; n+1 is first-order approximation
